Process and Manufacturing Projects

Statistics

Yield Optimization using Design of Experiments

01/2024 – 05/2024 | ASU
  • Designed a randomized three-factor full factorial experiment with 16 runs in JMP Pro to study how temperature, fermentation time, and fat content affect yield.
  • Analyzed results with ANOVA and regression: temperature and time were the significant yield drivers, while fat content and interactions were not.
  • Validated the model with residual analysis and recommended processing at about 40°C for 8 to 10 hours.

CAD and Assembly Work

3-Part Modular Automotive Vent Air Freshener

SolidWorks | designed for basic plastic injection molding and manual assembly

Exploded view: housing, scent pod core, vent clip

  • Main housing: front cover with radial ventilation slots positioned to direct airflow across the scent core.
  • Scent pod core: internal cartridge with through-hole air channels to maximize surface area exposure.
  • Vent clip and baseplate: rear clip dimensioned to grip standard automotive HVAC louvers with an interference friction fit.
  • Modeled parts with parametric sketching, revolves, and cut-extrusions; used concentric and coincident mates to verify alignment and clearances.
  • Created an exploded view to check disassembly and pod replacement access, and drafted 2D documentation with a bill of materials and key interface dimensions.

Universal Coupling Joint Assembly

SolidWorks | motion study and explode-collapse animation

  • Modeled the parts and applied mating constraints to build a working universal coupling joint assembly.
  • Set up a motion study to show the joint's rotation, alignment, and motion characteristics, plus an explode-collapse sequence to show how components relate.

Belt Roller Support Assembly

SolidWorks | explode and collapse animation

  • Built the assembly and animated its breakdown to show part placement and how each component fits into the final design.
  • Useful for assembly procedures, component relationships, and manufacturing documentation.
